title: Reducing Contextual Stochastic Bilevel Optimization via Structured Function Approximation
claim: A structured-basis reduction converges faster and more accurately than the baseline across loss, lower-level error and upper-level error.
layout: 3 line-plot panels, left-to-right, shared x-axis n with error bars
description: Three side-by-side line plots share the x-axis n, with values 3, 5, 10, 20, 30, 50 and 100 on a categorical scale. The left panel plots the loss F(x̄) with a dashed black reference line near 0.024. The center panel plots lower-level error Δy. The right panel plots upper-level error Δx. Each panel has the same four colored curves with error bars: stocBiO in blue, and the reduction with monomial (orange), Fourier (purple) and Chebyshev (green) bases. The blue baseline starts high and decays slowly as n grows. The reduced methods drop to near the reference or near zero by n=5 to 10. Monomial plateaus at a higher Δy than Fourier and Chebyshev. Legends sit in the top-right of each panel, and light grid lines run behind the curves.
caption: Loss $F(\bar{x})$ (left), lower level solution error $\Delta_y$ (center), and upper level solution error $\Delta_x$ (right) of stocBiO and our reduction framework using monomial, Fourier, and Chebyshev bases. The reference loss is $F_ref = F(x^\star)$.
abstract: Contextual Stochastic Bilevel Optimization (CSBO) extends standard stochastic bilevel optimization (SBO) by incorporating context-dependent lower-level problems. CSBO problems are generally intractable since existing methods require solving a distinct lower-level problem for each sampled context, resulting in prohibitive sample and computational complexity, in addition to relying on impractical conditional sampling oracles. We propose a reduction framework that approximates the lower-level solutions using expressive basis functions, thereby decoupling the lower-level dependence on context and transforming CSBO into a standard SBO problem solvable using only joint samples from the context and noise distribution. First, we show that this reduction preserves hypergradient accuracy and yields an $Îµ$-stationary solution to CSBO. Then, we relate the sample complexity of the reduced problem to simple metrics of the basis. This establishes sufficient criteria for a basis to yield $Îµ$-stationary solutions with a near-optimal complexity of $\widetilde{O}(Îµ^{-3})$, matching the best-known rate for standard SBO up to logarithmic factors. Moreover, we show that Chebyshev polynomials provide a concrete and efficient choice of basis that satisfies these criteria for a broad class of problems. Empirical results on inverse and hyperparameter optimization demonstrate that our approach outperforms CSBO baselines in convergence, sample efficiency, and memory usage.
